job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

passage: In our science lab today, we investigated the quality of water and air. We first examined a sample of clear, sparkling water from a local stream. Although it looked perfectly clean, our chemical test strips revealed high levels of dissolved pesticides and lead, proving that clear water can still contain invisible, dangerous toxins. We then discussed how to make water safe. We learned that while boiling kills germs, it cannot remove dissolved chemical pollutants. Next, we looked at the atmosphere. We discussed how the greenhouse effect is actually a natural process that keeps our planet warm enough for life. Without these gases, Earth would be too cold to inhabit. However, human activities are increasing these gases, leading to global warming. Finally, we analyzed air quality. We observed that even when air looks invisible and has no smell, it can contain harmful microscopic particles. We also clarified that smog is not just natural fog; it is a dangerous mixture of smoke and fog caused by industrial emissions and vehicle exhaust. Understanding these differences helps us realize that our senses are not enough to detect pollution, and that natural processes are often distorted by human actions.

items.evidence: Although it looked perfectly clean, our chemical test strips revealed high levels of dissolved pesticides and lead, proving that clear water can still contain invisible, dangerous toxins.
items.q: Meena's stream water looks clear and sparkling. What can she conclude about whether it is safe?
options: It may still hold hidden poisonous chemicals
It is safe because it looks so clean
It is unsafe only if it smells bad
It is safe since stream water is fresh
items.explain: The clear stream water still had pesticides and lead, so clear water can hide dangerous toxins.

wrong.why: thinks clear water is always safe to drink
trusts the senses, like believing odourless air is clean
ignores that the polluted sample came from a stream

items.evidence: We learned that while boiling kills germs, it cannot remove dissolved chemical pollutants.
items.q: A family boils stream water that contains lead. What does the boiling do?
options: It kills germs but leaves the lead in
It removes the lead along with the germs
It removes every kind of pollution in water
It turns the lead into harmless steam
items.explain: Boiling kills germs, but it cannot remove dissolved chemicals like lead.

wrong.why: thinks boiling removes chemicals like lead
thinks one treatment removes all pollution
thinks dissolved chemicals boil away with the water

items.evidence: Without these gases, Earth would be too cold to inhabit.
items.q: What would happen to Earth if all greenhouse gases suddenly disappeared?
options: It would be far too cold for life
It would stay as warm as it is now
It would be cooler and safer for life
It would get hotter as sunlight comes in
items.explain: Greenhouse gases keep Earth warm; without them it would be too cold to live on.

wrong.why: does not see that the gases keep Earth warm
thinks the greenhouse effect is only harmful
reverses the effect of the gases on heat

items.evidence: We also clarified that smog is not just natural fog; it is a dangerous mixture of smoke and fog caused by industrial emissions and vehicle exhaust.
items.q: How is smog different from the natural fog seen on a winter morning?
options: It is fog mixed with smoke from vehicles
It is just a much thicker kind of fog
It is fog formed only by cold air
It is safer to breathe than ordinary fog
items.explain: Smog is a dangerous mix of fog with smoke from factories and vehicle exhaust.

wrong.why: thinks smog is just thick winter fog
thinks smog has a natural cause, not human emissions
reverses the passage, which calls smog dangerous
